patch_description: The recommendation section suggests the top programs saturate because single-point moves cannot escape configurations where the smallest triangle is "trapped". I add coordinated group moves to the polish phase: with ~20% probability, simultaneously perturb all 3 vertices of the current smallest-area triangle with correlated Gaussian deltas scaled to the current step. Moving all three vertices together lets the triangle "translate/expand" as a unit — something impossible when moving points one at a time against a hard-min objective, since any single-vertex move typically increases some other triangle's deficiency first. Additionally, I bias the correlated component along the outward direction from the triangle's centroid (its natural expansion mode), which directly increases its area while the shared translation component keeps other areas roughly invariant. I also track the best-so-far configuration independently from the annealing current state, so worsening (escape) moves never destroy the incumbent. This targets pushing min_area from the ~0.01–0.03 plateau toward the ~0.037 benchmark.
